analysis.title: Future Quality Insights: is healthcare a Future Quality opportunity hiding in plain sight?
key_insights: Healthcare investors have had a poor few years: cyclicals beat defensives in 2023 and 2024, AI-related stocks then added pressure on defensives, and subsectors faced US policy uncertainty, a post-COVID investment lull and fears over AI. The author is increasingly optimistic that policy concerns are easing, investment is returning and AI is likely a tailwind.

Amova holds Eli Lilly in its Global Equity strategy and does not hold Novo Nordisk (now branded Novo). The firm rates company-level ability to sustain high returns on investment as more important than sector exposure.

Eli Lilly: under Chair and CEO Dave Ricks, management opened manufacturing capacity to meet GLP-1 demand while continuing to invest. The company made upwards of USD 20 billion in acquisitions in 2026 to prepare for growth into the next decade, and clinical trials continue to support its pipeline.

Novo: operational difficulty meeting demand has cost market share, pipeline execution has been mixed with high-profile setbacks, and investors question sales growth beyond semaglutide's patent expiry. At its recent capital markets day, management said it must step up business development and M&A but did not convince investors of a credible long-term path. Amova says catching up will not be easy or cheap and questions the direction of its future returns on investment.

Life sciences tools and services valuations fell significantly over three years for three reasons: a post-COVID air pocket in demand after capacity was added for vaccines, Trump administration attempts to cut US life science research spending, and fear that LLMs would disrupt the sector.

The NIH funding concern has been less damaging than feared. The 2025 draft budget proposed a 40% cut to NIH funding, but Congress kept funding at the prior year's level, and research funding has bipartisan support for increases.

Biotech funding is recovering, which benefits CROs and tools companies. The recovery is only a few months old and prior cycles suggest it runs several years. Interest rates and credit availability remain a variable to watch.

AI fears hit life science tools in February 2026 after an LLM began discussing life sciences applications. Amova argues the reaction was an overreaction: AI lets pharma test more targets (anecdotally up to a tenfold increase in molecules), and all of them need wet-lab proof of concept, which tools and services firms supply.
Amova expects AI to be a meaningful positive for life science tools and services. Real commercial applications of the technology are still a long way off.

Moderna and Merck's personalised mRNA cancer vaccine cut recurrence and spread of melanoma, and the market reaction was overwhelmingly positive, adding billions to each company's market capitalisation. mRNA must show efficacy in other tumour types, where it has worked poorly before, so Amova is cautiously optimistic.

Amova sees the pendulum swinging slowly back toward healthcare for diversification and for selective long-term growth and profitability. Its longest-held portfolio companies tap healthcare demand in ways that save money for health systems and deliver good patient outcomes. The thesis needs companies to show that lower regulatory pressure, successful AI deployment and more drug discoveries translate into earnings growth.

market_movers.rationale: Held in Amova's Global Equity strategy. Management has expanded manufacturing capacity for GLP-1 demand, made upwards of USD 20 billion of acquisitions this year, and the pipeline continues to progress in trials.
Not held by Amova. Lost market share on supply difficulty, mixed pipeline execution and an unconvincing capital markets day, with sales growth in question after semaglutide's patent expiry.
The joint personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine result with Merck was received overwhelmingly positively. Efficacy in other tumour types is still unproven.
The joint personalised mRNA melanoma vaccine result with Moderna added billions to its market capitalisation. Efficacy in other tumour types is still unproven.

sector_views.rationale: Policy concerns are easing, investment is returning and AI looks like a tailwind. The sector offers diversification and selective long-term growth. The report does not state an explicit overweight rating.

Recovery in biotech funding benefits CROs and tools companies, NIH funding was maintained, and AI-driven molecule discovery raises demand for wet-lab testing. The report does not state an explicit overweight rating.

tension_points.bull_case: Policy concerns are easing, biotech funding is returning, AI is boosting demand for tools and services through more targets tested, and positive trial data such as the Moderna and Merck melanoma vaccine is lifting interest.
tension_points.bear_case: The recovery is only a few months old, mRNA efficacy has to be shown in other tumour types, interest rates and credit availability could constrain funding, and companies must still convert these factors into earnings growth.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Companies fail to demonstrate that lower regulatory pressure, successful AI deployment and more drug discoveries translate into earnings growth.
